faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions

items.question: What are the common health issues in Nabha?
items.answer: People in Nabha often face lifestyle-related issues like diabetes, hypertension (high BP), heart problems, obesity, and seasonal diseases like dengue, viral fever, and respiratory infections.

items.question: How can I keep myself healthy on a daily basis?
items.answer: Eat a balanced diet (fruits, vegetables, pulses, milk). Drink clean water and avoid excessive junk food. Do at least 30 minutes of exercise daily (walking, yoga, cycling). Sleep for 7–8 hours regularly. Avoid smoking, alcohol, and tobacco.

items.question: Where can I go for medical help in Nabha?
items.answer: Government Hospitals & Community Health Centres, Private Clinics in the city, Pharmacies for basic medicines. In emergencies, call 108 Ambulance Service.

items.question: How can I prevent seasonal diseases like dengue and malaria?
items.answer: Don't let water collect in open containers. Use mosquito nets or repellents. Keep your surroundings clean and dry. Wear full-sleeved clothes in the rainy season.

items.question: What should I do if I feel symptoms of diabetes or high BP?
items.answer: Get your sugar and BP checked regularly at a nearby clinic. If you feel excessive thirst, frequent urination, headache, or dizziness, consult a doctor immediately. Follow the doctor's advice on diet, medicines, and lifestyle changes.

items.question: Are there any free health check-up camps in Nabha?
items.answer: Yes, from time to time the local government hospitals and NGOs organize free camps for blood pressure, sugar, eye check-ups, and vaccination drives. Stay updated through local news, panchayat announcements, or hospital notices.

items.question: How can I improve my children's health?
items.answer: Give them nutritious food (green veggies, milk, eggs, pulses). Ensure they get vaccinations on time. Encourage them to play outdoor games instead of only mobile/TV. Teach them handwashing and hygiene habits.

items.question: What mental health support is available in Nabha?
items.answer: Government hospitals have counselors and psychiatrists. You can also talk to local NGOs working in mental health. Simple steps like talking to family, meditation, yoga, and keeping a routine help improve mental well-being.

items.question: How do I know if the water I'm drinking is safe?
items.answer: Use boiled or filtered water. If water looks muddy or smells bad, avoid drinking. Contact the local municipal board for water supply issues.

items.question: Where can I get emergency help quickly?
items.answer: Dial 108 for Ambulance Service. Government Hospital, Nabha is the nearest emergency care provider. Keep a list of nearby private clinics and pharmacy numbers handy.
